name: Arc 3 8300G
analog: AMD Ryzen 3 8300G (docs only, never shown in game)
desc: A 4-core Socket V5 APU with built-in graphics, for a cheap first build without a graphics card.

unbox.packaging: ships in a clear plastic clamshell inside the retail box; nothing to peel on the part

doc_notes: Socket V5 only. Lift the socket lever fully before you place the Arc 3 8300G.
Line up the gold triangle on the corner of the CPU with the triangle on the socket. Never press the CPU in; it drops into place.
Lower the load plate and close the lever until it clicks under its hook. The socket cap pops off by itself: keep it in case the board goes back.
Thermal paste: one pea-sized dot (about 4 mm) in the centre of the heat spreader. The cooler's pressure spreads it.
TDP 65 W, package power up to 88 W. Pick a cooler rated for at least 88 W.
Built-in graphics: plug the monitor into the motherboard's video outputs when no graphics card is fitted.
4 cores / 8 threads, 3.4 GHz base, up to 4.9 GHz boost, 8 MB L3 cache.
Memory: DDR5 only. Install sticks in A2 and B2 first for two-stick kits.
Never touch the gold pads under the CPU or the pins in the socket.
Update the motherboard BIOS before first boot if the board is older than the CPU.

name: Arc Epoch 9124
analog: AMD EPYC 9124 (docs only, never shown in game)
desc: An entry 16-core server CPU for Socket SP-V, with 12 memory channels. Ships in its orange carrier.

unbox.carrier: A_CARRIER_0 stays on: the CPU is installed in its carrier
unbox.packaging: ships in a clamshell tray with the carrier already fitted

doc_notes: Pull the clear contact cover off the underside by its tab just before you install. Never touch the gold pads.
Keep the CPU in its orange carrier. Lift the socket's force frame and the rail frame, then slide the carrier into the rails until it stops.
Match the triangle on the carrier and the CPU corner with the triangle on the socket.
Lower the rail frame, close the force frame, then tighten its Torx T20 screws in the order 1-2-3 printed on the frame.
Thermal paste: most SP-V heatsinks come with a pre-applied pad. Otherwise spread a thin even layer over the whole heat spreader.
TDP 200 W. Use a heatsink rated for Socket SP-V and at least 200 W in a server with front-to-back airflow.
16 cores / 32 threads, 3.0 GHz base, up to 3.7 GHz, 64 MB L3 cache.
12 DDR5 RDIMM channels: fit one RDIMM per channel for full bandwidth. 128 PCIe 5.0 lanes.
Socket SP-V only; not compatible with desktop V5 boards.

name: Tiron Platinum 8480
analog: Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ (docs only, never shown in game)
desc: 56 cores on Socket L46, with 8 memory channels and built-in accelerators. Ships in its carrier clip.

unbox.carrier: A_CARRIER_0 stays on: the CPU is installed in its carrier
unbox.packaging: ships in a clamshell tray with the carrier already fitted

doc_notes: Pull the clear contact cover off the underside by its tab just before you install. Never touch the gold pads.
Snap the CPU into its black carrier clip with the triangles lined up, then clip the carrier onto the heatsink.
Lower the heatsink, CPU and clip onto the socket's four studs. It only fits one way round.
Tighten the four Torx T30 nuts in a cross pattern, 1-2-3-4, as printed on the heatsink label.
Thermal paste: heatsinks come with a pre-applied pad. Otherwise spread a thin even layer over the whole heat spreader.
TDP 350 W. Use a heatsink rated for Socket L46 and at least 350 W.
56 cores / 112 threads, 2.0 GHz base, up to 3.8 GHz, 105 MB cache.
8 DDR5 RDIMM channels: fit one RDIMM per channel for full bandwidth. 80 PCIe 5.0 lanes.
Socket L46 only; not compatible with desktop L17 boards.
